questions.question: The same operation(s) are followed in all the given number pairs except one. Find that odd number pair. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.questionHtml:
The same operation(s) are followed in all the given number pairs except one. Find that odd number pair.
(NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent
digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1
and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.solution:
Option 4) 72 : 12

12 × 6 + 2 = 72

72 + 2 = 72

74 ≠ 72 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Thus, out of all the options, '72 : 12' is the odd one out.

questions.question: Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some rats are mouse. No mouse is a rodent. Some rats are kittens. Conclusions: I. No rodent is a kitten. II. Some rats are rodent. III. No kitten is a mouse.
questions.questionHtml:
Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if
they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the
statements.
Statements:
Some rats are mouse.
No mouse is a rodent.
Some rats are kittens.
Conclusions:
I. No rodent is a kitten.
II. Some rats are rodent.
III. No kitten is a mouse.
questions.solution:
Conclusions:

(I) No rodent is a kitten→ Does not follow (As no mouse is a rodent and some rats are kittens. As no direct relation is given between rodent and Kitten, therefore it is false.)

(II) Some rats are rodent → Does not follow (As some rats are mouse and no mouse is a rodent. So it is possible but not definite.)

(III) No kitten is a mouse → Does not follow (As no mouse is a rodent and some rats are kittens. As no direct relation is given between mouse and Kitten, therefore it is false.)

questions.question: Two different positions of the same dice with faces R, P, T, S, M and B are shown below. Select the letter that will be on the face opposite to the one having S.
questions.questionHtml: Two different positions of the same dice with faces R, P, T, S, M and B are shown below. Select the letter that will be on the face opposite to the one having S.
questions.solution:
As S is common on both the dices, it is clear that R, T, P, and M are adjacent to it, and the remaining i.e. B will be opposite to it.

​

Opposite pairs:

R → P

T → M

S → B

So, the opposite side of "S" will be side "B".

questions.question: All of the letters in the word 'JUNGLE' are arranged in alphabetical order. How many letters are there in the English alphabetical series between the letter which is second from the left end and the one which is third from the right end in the new letter-cluster thus formed?
questions.questionHtml: All of the letters in the word 'JUNGLE' are arranged in alphabetical order. How many letters are there in the English alphabetical series between the letter which is second from the left end and the one which is third from the right end in the new letter-cluster thus formed?
questions.solution:
Given numbers J U N G L E
Arranged in English alphabetical order E G J L N U

The letter which is second from the left end and the one which is third from the right end in the new letter-cluster thus formed:

(Left end) E G J L N U (Right end) → G and L

Thus, the number of letters according to the English alphabetical series between G an L are four i.e. H, I, J and K.
